moat_against: Bundled 'good enough' rivals — GitHub Packages and GitLab, plus Sonatype Nexus, Harbor and hyperscaler registries (ECR/GCR/ACR) attack from inside platforms customers already pay for
No ROIC proof — roic_proxy negative every year 2020-2025 (FY2025 -8.9%); GAAP operating losses persist after SBC, so pricing power is unproven in filed numbers
Gross margin erosion — 83.1% in 2018 to 76.8% in FY2025 as cloud hosting costs grow with the SaaS mix (53% of Q2 2026 revenue)
SBC-funded talent model — SBC $156.7M in FY2025 exceeds all of OCF growth headroom and dilutes holders 5.4%/yr; the moat is re-bought annually in stock
moat_for: Artifactory dominance — the enterprise system of record for binaries/artifacts across 30+ package formats, with deep CI/CD integrations
Switching costs once artifact storage, replication, retention and release workflows sit on the platform; mission-critical and rarely ripped out
Expansion inside the base — net revenue retention 121% in Q2 2026, 1,291 customers >$100k ARR, 97 >$1M, Enterprise+ 59% of revenue
Security attach — Xray/supply-chain security is landing with new logos (>40% of Q2 2026 new wins included security) and the $1M+ cohort (>80%)
moat_justification: Artifactory is the dominant enterprise artifact repository and the system of record for software binaries, with real switching costs, 121% net revenue retention in Q2 2026 and 1,291 customers above $100k ARR — a genuine moderate moat. It is not 7+: the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json is negative in every year from 2020 to 2025 (FY2025 -8.9%) because GAAP operating income is negative after SBC, gross margin has slid from 83.1% (2018) to 76.8% (FY2025) on cloud hosting costs, and bundled 'good enough' artifact tools from GitHub and GitLab plus Sonatype and hyperscaler registries contest every renewal. No ROIC evidence of pricing power through a cycle exists yet.
